decision.summary: Two regions stand out: (1) a sharp, multi-axis step near index 478 affecting E and U strongly with N support, lacking an obvious return; (2) a brief but highly coherent linear trend across all axes starting at index 725, likely non-geophysical. Other segments show typical noise or smooth drift without ambiguous superposed changes.

regions.observation: Sharp ~10 MAD upward step in E (from ~0 to ~10) and simultaneous ~15 MAD downward step in U (from ~0 to ~-15) around index 478–479, with N showing a smaller concurrent drop (~2 MAD). The E and U steps appear coherent and abrupt across multiple samples; no clear opposing return is visible within the window, though E shows slight relaxation afterward.

From ~725 onward, all three components show large, correlated linear trends: N drops steadily (~1.2 MAD), E rises (~1.5 MAD), and U drops (~0.6 MAD) over just 5 indices. The lines are nearly straight and parallel in slope, suggesting a possible instrumental or processing artifact rather than physical motion; the abrupt onset at 725 (last window) warrants inspection despite minimal surrounding context.
